p: Now, when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos,
we do not blow the shofar (Rosh Hashanah 29b).
כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר זִכְרוֹן תְּרוּעָה (וַיִּקְרָא כג, כד),
וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר יוֹם תְּרוּעָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר כט, א);
and one verse says, 'a day of teruah' (Bamidbar 29:1);
we mention it but do not blow."
"If it is forbidden by Torah law,
how did they blow in the Mikdash?"
וְהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נִרְאֶה דְּלָא חָשׁ לָזֶה,
And the Midrash Rabbah seemingly is not concerned with this,
"'A day of teruah it shall be for you'
and it is a decree of the Torah.
"And furthermore, it is not a melachah,
that a verse should be needed to exclude it!"
And how would the Midrash Rabbah answer this?
אַךְ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת הִקְשׁוּ שָׁם (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל הָא):
"On the contrary: because it is not a melachah,
I would have thought that it is permitted;
so a verse was needed to exclude it";
and they answered this, see there.
It appears that the Midrash Rabbah holds
in line with the question of Tosafos,
and so they rightly expounded from "a remembrance of teruah"
that one does not blow on Shabbos outside the Mikdash,
but in the Mikdash they do blow;
and they expounded both verses as referring to Shabbos.
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְהָבִין טַעְמוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר.
But one must understand the reason for the matter.
Granted, according to what the Gemara says in its conclusion,
one can say that in the Mikdash they did not decree,
along the lines of what they said (Shabbos 20a):
and "there is no shevus in the Mikdash" (Beitzah 11b).
אֲבָל לְהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שֶׁהוּא גְּזֵרַת הַכָּתוּב,
But according to the Midrash Rabbah, that it is a decree of the Torah,
one must understand the reason for the matter.
the main intent of blowing the shofar,
as we have said (and as explained in the previous maamarim),
is to arouse fear in the heart,
אִם יִתָּקַע שׁוֹפָר בְּעִיר וְעָם לֹא יֶחֱרָדוּ.
"Shall a shofar be blown in a city and the people not tremble?"
וְהָרַמְבַּ״ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (הִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה ג, ד) כָּתַב:
And the Rambam, z"l (Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4), wrote:
"There is a hint in the matter:
Awake, you sleepers, from your slumber."
the pasuk "those who fear My Name" (Malachi 3:20)
as referring to those who keep Shabbos (as Rashi explains);
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ אָז לְשׁוֹפָר לְעוֹרֵר הַיִּרְאָה,
so then there is no need for a shofar to arouse fear,
and the reason does not apply,
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz."
And likewise in the holy Zohar,
where the reason for the order of the blasts is brought:
shevarim from the side of Yitzchak,
teruah from the side of Yaakov;
the lower Shechinah is the knot (kesher) of them all" —
דְּהַיְינוּ ק׳ תְּקִיעָה, ש׳ שְׁבָרִים, ר׳ תְּרוּעָה
that is, Kuf for tekiah, Shin for shevarim, Reish for teruah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רלב, א).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַתְּקִיעוֹת מְעוֹרְרִין זֶה
That is, through the blasts we arouse this:
that Yisrael are crowned with the Avos.
And about this it is said (Tehillim 89:16),
"Fortunate is the people who know the teruah,"
וְלֹא כְּתִיב שׁוֹמְעֵי אוֹ תּוֹקְעֵי תְּרוּעָה,
and it is not written "who hear" or "who blow" the teruah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדִּקְדְּקוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם רלא, ב),
as they inferred in the holy Zohar (ibid. 231b);
וְכֵן דִּקְדְּקוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כט, ד):
and so they inferred in the Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 29:4):
וְכִי אֵין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יוֹדְעִין לְהָרִיעַ?
"Do the nations of the world not know how to sound a teruah?
how many trumpets they have, etc.!
how to win over their Creator with the teruah, etc."
who know the supernal secrets of their Master,
to enter before Him and to bind themselves to Him, etc.;
they will draw near to walk in the light of the countenance
And what it says, "and to bind themselves to Him" —
the intent is as it hinted afterward
And "to walk in the light of His countenance, etc." —
הַכַּוָּנָה עַל לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים פט, טז)
the intent is the language of the verse (Tehillim 89:16),
"Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they will walk."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שָׁם קיט, א)
And it is in the manner of what is said (ibid. 119:1),
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
means to be bound to the root;
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
and this is when there is the unity of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם רלב, א):
as written in the holy Zohar (ibid. 232a):
the Shechinah from HaKadosh Baruch Hu."
And the unity of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah
הוּא רַק כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ יִחוּד בְּחִינַת אַבָּא וְאִמָּא,
comes only when there is the unity of the aspect of Abba and Imma,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קט, ב).
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 109b).
וְכֵן זֶה מוֹרֶה קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין,
And likewise the knot of tefillin indicates this,
that Yisrael are bound to the root.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לְמִצְוַת שׁוֹפָר בְּשַׁבָּת,
And for this reason the mitzvah of shofar has no place on Shabbos,
the Shin is the secret of the three Avos,
and the Bas (daughter) is crowned with them."
And the essence of the shofar is, as we said,
to be "those who know the teruah,"
the great shofar, which is Binah,
so that there be the unity of Abba and Imma
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צט, ב).
And on Shabbos one can also
וּבְכָל הַיּוֹם יֵשׁ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ;
and throughout the day there is the unity of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah;
for the whole day one is like one who does a mitzvah,
since he is like one to whom a matter of sin came
and he was saved from it,
who is like one who does a mitzvah
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
and as a matter of course there is the unity of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah,
and there is no further need for the mitzvah of shofar
Also, Shabbos is not a time for tefillin,
for they themselves are a sign
and this is because he goes about
בְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם כָּל הַיּוֹם.
in acceptance of the yoke of Heaven's kingship all day.
he is like one who goes all day in tefillin.
וְעוֹד אָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פִּנְחָס שָׁם, רלא, ב):
And further it says in the holy Zohar (Pinchas, ibid. 231b):
"And all those who know the secret of the teruah
יִתְקָרְבוּן לְמֵיהַךְ בְּאוֹר פָּנָיו דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
will draw near to walk in the light of the countenance of HaKadosh Baruch Hu;
and this is the primordial light
דְּגָנִיז קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְצַדִּיקַיָּיא וְכוּלֵּי.
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu hid away for the righteous, etc."
And concerning Shabbos it is brought in Sefer HaBahir (160):
"He took a seventh and set it for them in its place,
and the rest He hid away for the righteous, etc.";
for on Shabbos we merit to attain something of the hidden light,
as we say, "His light will rest upon it,"
and we also merit to be
"in the light of Your countenance they will walk."
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לִתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר בְּשַׁבָּת
And for this reason blowing the shofar has no place on Shabbos
(and why they blow in the Mikdash will be explained below).
